# Studio Draft examples and execution scope

The extension `.frog` does not select one language authority. Each example declares its document profile in the shared index, and this export checks that declaration against the actual file bytes. It never renames keys or converts a file to another profile.

| Index profile | Actual envelope | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `studio-draft` | `format: "frog.document.draft"`, integer `draft_revision`, Studio `frontPanel` | Product authoring document; execution requires the actual admitted native provider |
| `source-0.1` | `spec_version: "0.1"` | Public FROG Source with its existing validation, lowering and backend admission |

Draft revision, application version and public Source compatibility version are different identities. The copied Studio Draft files are not thereby published as public Source programs. Keeping the format unchanged is deliberate; successful execution of one graph does not admit all overloads of its functions.

Observed Studio Draft revisions in this index: `2, 4, 6, 7`. This observation is not a new revision-admission rule.

The index and explanations describe expectations. This documentation export does not run Studio, test the ABI, or certify a backend. It does not publish a Git commit or deployment. NativeFast/NativeDebuggable, explicit private Simulation, persistence, interactive actions and expected failures retain their separate meanings.

Download files individually while retaining their index-relative paths. The only copied binary dependency reviewed by this exporter is the corpus's C sample library, accompanied by its own sources, header, build recipe and the corpus repository license. No private preparation archive, developer SDK or application binary is redistributed.

[Browse the actual examples](../examples/index.md).
